literal: Yet the substance of soothing guidance lies in gain and loss among men.
idiomatic: Yet soothing the people rests on the men who govern them.

literal: One may again choose careful officials with weight, investigate and forbid according to law, and should not lightly alter laws and statutes or cut and dismiss the host of offices.
idiomatic: Choose careful officials, investigate by law, and do not lightly rewrite statutes or purge the ranks of office.

literal: Now we ask to reform the regulatory articles and return them to attachment under the code.
idiomatic: We ask to revise the regulatory articles and return them to the code proper.

literal: Those who encourage themselves in public integrity receive the regular reward; those in whom popular songs charge bribery are ranked in the review grade.
idiomatic: Let integrity earn the regular reward and bribery heard in popular song enter the review grade."

literal: Emperor Xiaozong followed this.
idiomatic: Xiaozong accepted the memorial.

literal: The night Xiang received the appointment, a violent wind with thunder and lightning uprooted a paulownia in his courtyard more than ten spans around and set it upright again at its root.
idiomatic: The night Xiang took the appointment, a thunderstorm uprooted a ten-span paulownia in his courtyard and set it upright again at the root.

literal: At first, when Xiaozong took the reins of government, Xiang heard that Prince of Pengcheng Xi had the worry of shaking the ruler, and wished to seize his Ministry of Works post; he greatly feared public talk and therefore made him grand general; only now did he occupy it.
idiomatic: When Xiaozong first took power, Xiang had heard Xi of Pengcheng might overshadow the throne and wished to seize his ministry; fearing talk, he made Xi grand general instead—and only now took the post himself.

literal: Heaven's might was thus; those who knew saw he would not reach the end.
idiomatic: Heaven had spoken; those who knew saw he would not finish his course.

literal: Xiaozong held martial exercises at Ye; Xiang together with Right Vice Director Gao Zhao and Army Commander Yu Jin remained to guard the capital.
idiomatic: Xiaozong drilled troops at Ye; Xiang, Right Vice Director Gao Zhao, and Army Commander Yu Jin stayed to guard Luoyang.

literal: At first, at the end of Taihe, Xiang as the youngest brother received prolonged favor; at the beginning of Jingming, again as youngest paternal uncle he received exalted favor—position and expectation reached the utmost, and the hundred offices feared him.
idiomatic: At Taihe's end he was the youngest brother and long favored; at Jingming's start he was the youngest paternal uncle and doubly exalted—rank and expectation peaked, and the hundred offices feared him.

literal: Yet he was greedy without satiety and took in much;
idiomatic: Yet he was insatiably greedy and took in much;

literal: in public and private he traded goods and stripped near and far;
idiomatic: public and private trade stripped near and far;

literal: he doted on petty men and everywhere received entreaties.
idiomatic: he doted on petty men and took petitions everywhere.

literal: Rare objects filled his halls, sound and color ran to excess, he built and adorned mansions and opened hills and pools—the cost reached tens of thousands.
idiomatic: Treasures filled his halls, music and women ran riot, mansions and artificial hills cost tens of thousands.

literal: Again outside the Eastern Flank Gate, south of the great road, he drove off common people and planned to seize residences.
idiomatic: Outside the Eastern Flank Gate, south of the great road, he drove out commoners to seize houses.

literal: There were even mourning biers in the hall; they asked delay until burial and were not permitted; he then had the coffin placed in the lane, and passersby sighed in grief.
idiomatic: Some still had mourning biers in the hall; they begged delay until burial and were refused; he set the coffin in the lane, and wayfarers wept.

literal: Xiang's mother Grand Consort Gao also helped in acts of violence; she personally ordered beatings, and cries of resentment rose everywhere.
idiomatic: His mother, Grand Consort Gao, aided his cruelty; she ordered beatings herself, and cries of resentment filled the streets.

literal: As consort, daughter of Prince of Song Liu Chang, she was not answered with ritual courtesy.
idiomatic: Consort to him, daughter of Prince of Song Liu Chang, she received no ritual courtesy in return.

literal: His favored concubine Lady Fan was loved equal to his wife; when she died he could not master his grief, and even after burial he still ruined the coffin to gaze upon her.
idiomatic: His concubine Lady Fan was loved like a wife; when she died his grief would not end, and even after burial he broke open the coffin to look on her.

literal: He memorialized asking posthumous enfeoffment as Lady of Pingchang county.
idiomatic: He asked posthumously to enfeoff her as lady of Pingchang county.

literal: Xiang again had illicit relations with Lady Gao, consort of Prince of Anding Ye, and Lady Gao was the elder sister of Ru Hao's wife.
idiomatic: Xiang also lay with Lady Gao, consort of Prince of Anding Ye—Ru Hao's wife's elder sister.

literal: He strictly forbade those at his side and kept the matter closed from beginning to end.
idiomatic: He silenced his household and kept the affair secret from first to last.

literal: Xiang had long been attached to Hao, and again because of licentious liking, their coming and going was close.
idiomatic: Long attached to Hao, and bound by the affair, they grew intimate.

literal: When Hao took a wife, Xiang personally went to his house, drank with delight, and reached extreme drunkenness.
idiomatic: When Hao married, Xiang went to his house in person, drank with delight, and staggered home drunk.

literal: Though Xiang's greed and excess in gathering wealth were known to court and countryside, yet Xiaozong's ritual respect remained lofty and his trust unbroken; he gathered military and state great affairs and decided them in total.
idiomatic: Though his greed was known throughout court and countryside, Xiaozong's courtesy never slackened nor his trust broke; military and state affairs passed through his hands.

literal: Whenever he presented memorials, matters all accorded with approval.
idiomatic: Whatever he memorialized was approved.

literal: Xiang often lodged separately in the western corner of Hualin Park, adjoining the capital pavilion and palace lodgings in close proximity, and also had passage through the rear gate.
idiomatic: He often lodged in the western corner of Hualin Park, hard by the capital lodges, with a private passage through the rear gate.

literal: Xiaozong often secretly visited his place and drank freely all day—such was his favor.
idiomatic: Xiaozong often stole to his house and drank the day through—such was his favor.

literal: Again when Xiang received appointment, on a private celebration he opened a request to Xiaozong.
idiomatic: When he took a new appointment he used a private celebration to petition Xiaozong.

literal: Xiaozong often visited the Southern Residence, entered the rear hall, and met Grand Consort Gao, calling her "little mother"; he knelt and offered wine, with ritual like family.
idiomatic: Xiaozong often visited the Southern Residence and entered the rear hall to see Grand Consort Gao, calling her little mother; kneeling, he offered wine like kin.

literal: On leaving, Gao always bowed in send-off, raising the cup in blessing and saying: "May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years; year by year come once to this mother-and-son house.
idiomatic: On leaving, Gao always bowed him out, cup raised, praying: "May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years and year by year come once to our house."

literal: " At first when Xiaozong personally took government, Xiang together with Prince of Xianyang Xi and Prince of Pengcheng Xi were all summoned in, riding together in a calf cart, with guards strict and solid.
idiomatic: When Xiaozong first took power, Xiang, Xi of Xianyang, and Xi of Pengcheng were summoned together in a guarded calf cart.

literal: Gao at the time was in panic and thought Xiang would surely die; she also rode a carriage by a side road, weeping as she sent him to Jinfeng.
idiomatic: Gao, panicked, thought Xiang would die; she took a side road in her carriage, weeping as she followed him to Jinfeng.

literal: When Xiang escaped harm, Gao said: "From now on I do not wish wealth and honor—only that mother and son may preserve one another and sweep the market with you for a living.
idiomatic: When Xiang was spared, Gao said, "From now on I want no wealth—only that mother and son may live and sweep the market with you."

literal: " By now favor and exaltation were lofty and grand, and she no longer spoke of the principle of disaster and ruin.
idiomatic: By then favor had risen so high she no longer spoke of ruin.

literal: Later he was slandered by Gao Zhao, who said Xiang with Hao and others plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: Later Gao Zhao slandered him, saying Xiang and Hao plotted rebellion.

literal: At that time Xiang was at the Southern Residence; Xiaozong summoned Chief Commandant Cui Liang into the forbidden precinct and ordered investigation of Xiang's greed and licentiousness and the acts of monopoly by Hao, Liu Zhou, Chang Jixian, Chen Saojing, and others.
idiomatic: Xiang was then at the Southern Residence; Xiaozong summoned Chief Commandant Cui Liang and ordered inquiry into Xiang's greed and lust and the monopolies of Hao, Liu Zhou, Chang Jixian, Chen Saojing, and the rest.

literal: Liang then memorialized against Xiang: "Greedy harm to public and private, licentious disorder of ritual canon.
idiomatic: Liang memorialized: "Greedy harm to public and private, licentious breach of ritual."

literal: The court of late, because military and state expenses were heavy, forbade miscellaneous tribute from all fiefs, yet Xiang on his own authority made awesome orders and commanded the offices to pay compensation.
idiomatic: "The court lately forbade tribute from the fiefs because expenses were heavy, yet Xiang on his own authority ordered offices to pay him compensation."

literal: He drove off and seized others' livelihoods and made his private residence extravagant.
idiomatic: "He seized livelihoods and built a lavish private house."

literal: Filthy violation without the Way, losing the integrity of high and low;
idiomatic: "Filthy violations broke the order of high and low;"

literal: he defiled and ruined the statutes and damaged the record of wind and teaching.
idiomatic: "he defiled the statutes and ruined the teaching of custom."

literal: We ask that according to the present matter he be removed from office and noble rank held, delivered to the Court for Dependencies for stripping, forthwith placed under prohibition, and delivered to the Court of Judicial Review for punishment.
idiomatic: "We ask that he be removed from office and rank, stripped by the Court for Dependencies, placed under prohibition, and handed to the Court of Judicial Review."

literal: " He also impeached Hao and the others; that night they were taken and confined at the Southern Terrace.
idiomatic: He also impeached Hao and the others; that night they were seized at the Southern Terrace.

literal: Again a hundred tiger guards surrounded and guarded Xiang's residence, fearing he would be startled and flee.
idiomatic: A hundred tiger guards surrounded his house lest he flee in panic.

literal: He sent his attendant Guo Yi to open the Jinfeng Gate, gallop out to announce to him, and show him the chief commandant's impeachment.
idiomatic: He sent Guo Yi to open the Jinfeng Gate, gallop out with the impeachment, and read it to him.

literal: Xiang's mother Gao saw Yi, beat her head on the ground and wailed beyond mastering herself.
idiomatic: Gao saw Yi, beat her head on the ground, and wailed beyond control.

literal: Xiang said: "If it is truly as the chief commandant impeaches, what is there to worry? I only fear a greater crime may fall upon me across the way.
idiomatic: Xiang said, "If it is truly as Liang impeaches, what is there to fear? I only dread a greater crime falling from nowhere."

literal: People offer me rare and strange goods; I truly love them.
idiomatic: "People give me rare goods and I truly love them."

literal: If it proves to be taking and receiving, what do I have to worry about?
idiomatic: "If it proves to be bribes, what do I have to fear?"

literal: " He privately comforted himself thus.
idiomatic: He comforted himself thus in private.

literal: By daylight Hao and the others were all sentenced to death; the five princes including Prince of Gaoyang Yong were led in to deliberate Xiang's crime.
idiomatic: At dawn Hao and the others were executed; Yong of Gaoyang and four other princes were called in to judge Xiang's crime.

literal: A single carriage guarded him; he returned to the Hualin lodge.
idiomatic: A single carriage guarded him back to the Hualin lodge.

literal: Mother and wife wept together and entered where he dwelt; a few young male slaves and weak maids followed.
idiomatic: Mother and wife wept and entered his lodging with only a few young slaves and weak maids.

literal: Official guards were very strict; all night the watch-clapper sounded, guards sat in ranks surrounding him, and inside and outside did not communicate.
idiomatic: Guards were severe; watch-clappers sounded all night, ranks sat round him, and none passed in or out.

literal: Xiaozong for this was unhappy in the park more than ten days.
idiomatic: For this Xiaozong kept to the park in sorrow more than ten days.

literal: Xiang was moved to the Court of the Imperial Treasury; the surrounding prohibition grew tighter.
idiomatic: Xiang was moved to the Court of the Imperial Treasury under tighter confinement.

literal: An edict said: "The prince's rank joins terrace and aide, his close kindness without second; court and countryside rely on him, the object of all eyes.
idiomatic: An edict said, "Your rank joins terrace and aide, your kinship without second; court and countryside rely on you."

literal: He could not encourage virtue and preserve the Way, spread and blend the track of instruction, but instead indulged this greedy shamelessness, foul violence plain to hear.
idiomatic: "You could not encourage virtue or spread instruction, but indulged greedy shame and violence plain to all."

literal: Far he failed the former court's charge of friendly love; near he betrayed the family's expectation of mutual respect; the law officers hold the statutes—truly it fits the penal canon; the realm is public—how can private favor be allowed?
idiomatic: "You failed the former emperor's trust and the family's respect; the law officers rightly invoke the code, and the realm is public—private favor cannot stand."

literal: But my several paternal uncles have fallen; those who remain are few; to pursue to the utmost in punishment—feeling has not yet been at ease.
idiomatic: "Yet my paternal uncles have fallen and few remain; to punish to the utmost my heart is not at ease."

literal: He may be removed to commoner status, a separate lodge and residence provided, guarded according to law, limited to his lifetime.
idiomatic: "You may be reduced to commoner status, given a separate lodge, guarded by law, for life."

literal: The state is ill-formed; words seek after sighs.
idiomatic: "The state is unlucky; I sigh as I write."

literal: " Thereupon a separate lodge was built in the northeast corner of Luoyang county; in twenty days it was finished, and he was to be moved to dwell there.
idiomatic: A lodge was built in the northeast of Luoyang county; in twenty days it was finished and he was to be moved there.

literal: Then several of his household slaves secretly formed a party and wished to seize Xiang out by force; they secretly copied names and secretly entrusted a serving maid to convey it to Xiang.
idiomatic: Then several household slaves secretly banded to seize him out by force, copied names, and sent word through a maid.

literal: Xiang had just taken it to read when the gate-guard chief saw from afar, burst in, and snatched from Xiang's hand what he held and presented it in memorial.
idiomatic: Xiang had just taken the note when the gate chief saw from afar, rushed in, snatched it from his hand, and memorialized.

literal: By night the guards reported it.
idiomatic: That night the guards reported it.

literal: Xiang cried several sounds and died suddenly.
idiomatic: Xiang cried out several times and died suddenly.

literal: [17] From the time Xiang reached the Court of the Imperial Treasury, he ordered his mother and wife to return to dwell at the Southern Residence, coming once every five days to meet with him.
idiomatic: [17] From his confinement at the Court of the Imperial Treasury, his mother and wife dwelt at the Southern Residence and visited every five days.

literal: This night mother and wife were not present; he died in a maid's hands.
idiomatic: That night mother and wife were absent; he died in a maid's hands.

literal: By daylight they announced the grievous news.
idiomatic: At dawn they announced his death.

literal: An edict said: "Beihai, my paternal uncle, has suddenly leaned his back in death; painful longing and drawn sobs—feeling cannot bear itself.
idiomatic: An edict said, "Beihai, my uncle, has suddenly fallen; grief and sobs I cannot master."

literal: Tomorrow let mourning be raised; order the funeral prepared and the coffin returned to the Southern Residence; all princes of the imperial clan are to hurry and attend.
idiomatic: "Raise mourning tomorrow; prepare the funeral and return the coffin to the Southern Residence; let all imperial princes attend."

literal: Give eastern-garden secret vessels; the number of funeral gifts all according to the Guangling precedent."
idiomatic: "Grant eastern-garden secret vessels; funeral gifts as for Guangling."

literal: When Xiang was first confined, he then told his mother of the affair with Lady Gao.
idiomatic: When first confined, he told his mother of the affair with Lady Gao.

literal: His mother was greatly angry and reviled him bitterly, saying: "You yourself have wife, concubine, and serving maids, in youth flourishing like flowers—why suddenly share illicit relations with that Goryeo slave woman and bring this crime?
idiomatic: His mother raged and cursed him: "You have wives and maids in their bloom—why lie with that Goryeo woman and bring this ruin?"

literal: If I get that Goryeo woman I shall eat her flesh.
idiomatic: "Catch that Goryeo woman and I will eat her flesh."

literal: " She then beat Xiang's back and both legs more than a hundred strokes, wielding the staff herself until strength failed and she ordered a slave to take her place.
idiomatic: She beat his back and both legs more than a hundred times, wielding the staff herself until spent, then had a slave continue.

literal: Lady Gao had always been strict; for every slight fault Xiang was often punished and rebuked, the staff wrapped in cotton.
idiomatic: Lady Gao had always been strict; for small faults she often beat him with a cotton-wrapped staff.

literal: Now the cotton was removed and all reached festering sores.
idiomatic: Now the cotton was removed and every blow brought festering sores.

literal: Xiang, tormented by the beating, was only after more than ten days able to stand.
idiomatic: Tormented by the beating, he could stand only after ten days.

literal: Again she beat his consort Lady Liu several tens of strokes, saying: "New wife of a great house, her gate and household matched in rank—what is there to fear that she does not inspect and restrain her husband?
idiomatic: She also beat his consort Lady Liu several dozen times: "A great-house bride, matched in rank—why not restrain your husband?"

literal: All women are jealous—are you alone not jealous!
idiomatic: "All women are jealous—are you alone not jealous?"

literal: " Lady Liu smiled and accepted punishment, and in the end said nothing.
idiomatic: Lady Liu smiled, took the blows, and said nothing.

literal: Though Xiang's faults of greed and licentiousness were heard far and near, on the day of his death his crimes had no fixed name, and far and near sighed in wonder.
idiomatic: Though his greed and lust were known far and near, at his death no fixed charge was named, and men marveled.

literal: The coffin lay in state five years.
idiomatic: His coffin lay in state five years.

literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongping an edict said: "The former Grand Tutor, Prince of Beihai, sprang from the former emperor, was especially cherished in friendly love, received the testamentary charge to assist, and the tender years are recorded.
idiomatic: In Yongping year one, tenth month, an edict said, "The late Grand Tutor, Prince of Beihai, sprang from the former emperor, was cherished in friendship, received the testament to assist the tender years."

literal: We did not expect his evening years would hide virtue and end lacking mournful honor; he may now be posthumously restored to princely enfeoffment, on a set day interred, slightly to comfort the shade
idiomatic: "We did not expect his late years would hide virtue and end without mourning honor; restore his princedom, bury him on a set day, and comfort the shade"

literal: 〈doubt〉
idiomatic: 〈doubt〉

literal: of kin.
idiomatic: of kin."

literal: Posthumous title Prince Ping.
idiomatic: Posthumous title: Prince Ping.

literal: His son Hao, courtesy name Ziming, inherited.
idiomatic: His son Hao, courtesy name Ziming, inherited.

literal: In youth he was generous and had bold spirit.
idiomatic: Young, he was generous and bold.

literal: He was appointed Dragon-Surging General and Unhampered Cavalier Attendant.
idiomatic: He was made dragon-surging general and unhampered cavalier attendant.

literal: He was transferred to Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, Grand Master of Splendor, long concurrent Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, Cavalier Attendant, and General Who Pacifies the East.
idiomatic: He became director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, grand master of splendor, long concurrent in that directorate, cavalier attendant, and general who pacifies the east.

literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Justice and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: He was made director of the Ministry of Justice with the additional title general who pacifies the south.

literal: He went out as Cavalier Attendant, Pacification-General, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: He was sent out as cavalier attendant, pacification-general, and inspector of Xuzhou.

literal: Before long the censor impeached him and he was removed from the register of names.
idiomatic: Soon the censor impeached him and he was struck from the rolls.

literal: Afterward the bandit chiefs Su Qin Mingda, Chigan Qilin, and others raided and disturbed Bin, Hua, and other provinces; then Hao's princely rank was restored, and with his present generalship he was given commissioner with credentials, acting General Who Campaigns West, commander of all military affairs of Hua, Bin, and East Qin, concurrent Left Vice Director, and Western-Route Mobile Office, to campaign against Mingda.
idiomatic: Later the chiefs Su Qin Mingda and Chigan Qilin raided Bin and Hua; Hao's princedom was restored, and with his present rank he was commissioner with credentials, acting general who campaigns west, commander of Hua, Bin, and East Qin armies, concurrent left vice director, and western-route mobile office, to campaign against Mingda.

literal: Hao turned and fought forward, repeatedly breaking the bandit hosts and relieving the sieges of Bin and Hua.
idiomatic: Hao fought forward, repeatedly broke the rebels, and lifted the sieges of Bin and Hua.
